title: Without -P the client follows its own patching default and contacts the patch host its PatchConfig.xml names
notes: The launcher prepares the run folder with --prepare and starts nothing, and the driver starts the client from
the launcher's own command with only its -P 0 taken out, so the client does what it does by default.
Without -P the client runs PatchClientInterface::StartPatching, which reads PatchConfig.xml from the folder it
runs in; the launcher's run folder holds none, so the driver copies the install's own Bin/PatchConfig.xml into
it with only the patch host and port changed, to 127.0.0.2 and 12700, where a local listener waits. The client
reaching that listener shows it contacts the patch host its PatchConfig.xml names by default, without any
connection to KingsIsle: the guard still ends the client at any connection off this machine.
127.0.0.2 is used because the client replaces 127.0.0.1 with this machine's own address before it connects,
which a first run showed when the listener on 127.0.0.1 saw nothing and the client dialled 12700 on the machine's
other interface. Nobody may type into the client during the run: a login it is refused opens a KingsIsle page on quit.
No game server runs here, so the login server's two warnings about empty creation and realm tables are expected.
server_log_allowed: character_create_school holds no school, so no wizard can be created until it does
realmlist holds no realm, so no player can be sent to a gameserver until one is added
